Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 Hon'Ble Smt Justice Tirumala Devi Eada
 LAAS.No.15 Of 2012
Judgment:
(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili)
Aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 23.02.2001 passed in O.P.No.5 of 1995 by the Senior Civil Judge, Miryalguda, the present Appeal has been filed by the appellant.

2. Heard learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant and Sri M.Venkat Ram Reddy, learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.1, 8, 10, 11, 13, 15 to 23.
3. It is the case of the appellant that the land to an extent of Ac.05.10 guntas situated at Anumula Village, was acquired for Nagarjuna Sagar Left Canal work from the respondents in pursuance of the Notification dated 06.06.1983 issued under Section 4 (1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act').
The Land Acquisition Officer has passed an Award on 22.02.1986 and fixed the market value at Rs.1500/- per acre for dry land and Rs.2,000/- per acre for converted wet land.

Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer, the respondents sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the Land Acquisition Officer has referred the case to the Reference Court and the same was numbered as O.P.No.5 of 1995.
Without appreciating any of the contentions raised by the appellant, the Reference Court vide judgment dated 23.02.2001 enhanced the compensation to Rs.45,000/- per acre.
Hence, the present appeal.

4. Learned Government Pleader appearing for the appellant had contended that there was no basis for the Reference Court to enhance the compensation from Rs.1,500/- per acre for dry land and Rs.2,000/- per acre for converted wet land to Rs.45,000/- per acre.
Therefore, appropriate orders be passed in the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree dated 23.02.2001 passed by the Reference Court in O.P.No.15 of 2012.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent Nos.1, 8, 10, 11, 13, 15 to 23 had contended that the Reference Court has relied upon Exs.A1 & A2-sale deeds, dated 14.06.1979 & 20.06.1983.
As per the said sale deeds, the lands were sold for a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- per acre and the lands acquired are situated in the same vicinity.

Therefore, the Reference Court has rightly enhanced the compensation and also granted additional market value, interest, and statutory benefits as the lands were acquired for Nagarjuna Sagar Left Canal.

The Reference Court has passed a reasoned order while enhancing The Land Acquisition Officer vs C.Ramulamma on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129133205/
1 the compensation and there are no merits in the appeal and the same is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: 6. Having considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel on either side, this Court is of the view that the Reference Court has rightly enhanced the compensation from Rs.1,500/- per acre for dry land and Rs.2,000/- per acre for converted wet land to Rs.45,000/- per acre by relying on Exs.A1 and A2, which discloses that the lands were sold @ Rs.1,20,000/- per acre.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the order passed by the Reference Court.
7. Accordingly, the Appeal is dismissed.
No costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
__ JUSTICEABHINAND KUMAR SHAVILI ________________________________ JUSTICE TIRUMALA DEVI EADA Date: 12.03.2025 rkk
